title: Serving-throughput evidence replaces assumed throughput in GPU quotes
summary: EVR-0017 showed that GPU-vs-API quotes depend almost entirely on the throughput input, which was assumed. throughput.py stores observations (model, revision, gpu, engine, kind generation|training, tokens/s, concurrency, source measured|benchmark|assumed) in <home>/throughput.jsonl; best() prefers measured over benchmark over assumed evidence, newest first; lookup() matches a GPU offer by display name or id. measure() benchmarks a registered OpenAI-compatible endpoint with N concurrent requests (temperature 0, fixed prompt and max_tokens) and computes aggregate completion tokens per wall-clock second from server-reported usage, plus per-request tokens/s; it is a real call only to the operator's own endpoint. compute.gpu_options accepts a per-offer rate function, prices only GPUs with evidence, and labels each option's throughput_source (explicit/measured). CLI: `orchestrate throughput measure|record|show`, `orchestrate quote --gpu-from runpod --model <id>`. Tested end-to-end against a local stdlib HTTP server implementing the OpenAI chat-completions shape.

prior_art.checked: PA-vllm (its own benchmark scripts report throughput), PA-skypilot (catalog prices, not throughput)
prior_art.found: serving engines ship offline benchmarks; Agent OS still needs per-endpoint evidence tied to its quotes
prior_art.reused: OpenAiCompatibleAdapter request/POST path; secret_refs for keyed endpoints
prior_art.why_custom: a small concurrent client and a JSONL store; vLLM benchmark numbers can be recorded with source=benchmark
